02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
A Chief Information Security Officer is appointed to oversee the entity's cyber security program and the cyber security for the entity's most critical technology resources.
Required because PSPF Release 2025 makes accountable cyber leadership mandatory for entity cyber security programs and critical technology resources.
Direct - applies to governance of Agency and Scheme Applications, their supporting platforms and critical application services.

NDIA must maintain a CISO role with oversight of cyber security obligations for Agency and Scheme Applications, including direction for security controls, assurance, exceptions and escalation of material application risks.

02. Entity Protective Security Roles and Responsibilities
The Chief Information Security Officer is accountable to the Accountable Authority for cyber security risks and how the entity's cyber security program is managing these risks.
Required to ensure the CISO is accountable to the Accountable Authority for cyber risks and the effectiveness of the cyber security program.
Direct - establishes executive accountability for application security risks and residual-risk reporting.
The CISO must report material Agency and Scheme Application cyber risks, control gaps, exceptions and treatment progress to the Accountable Authority or delegated governance forum.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
Procedures are developed, implemented and maintained to ensure security incidents are responded to and managed.
Incident response procedures are mandatory so security incidents affecting applications are detected, escalated, contained, remediated and evidenced.
Direct - applies to incidents involving Agency and Scheme Applications, data, integrations, users and suppliers.
NDIA must define, test and maintain procedures for identifying, triaging, escalating and managing security incidents that affect Agency and Scheme Applications or their information.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
Security incident management and response plans are incorporated into the entity's business continuity arrangements.
Mandatory because application security incidents can disrupt critical services and must be integrated with business continuity arrangements.
Direct - applies where application outages or compromise affect participant, provider or agency services.
Security incident response plans for Agency and Scheme Applications must align with business continuity, disaster recovery and crisis management arrangements for critical services.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
Significant or externally reportable security incidents and referral obligations are reported to the relevant authority (or authorities) within the applicable timeframe.
Required to meet external reporting obligations and mandated timeframes for significant security incidents.
Direct - applies to significant or externally reportable incidents involving applications, ICT services or protected information.
NDIA must define reportable incident thresholds, responsible roles and timeframes for notifying relevant authorities when Agency and Scheme Applications are affected.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Governance, accountability, risk and investment oversight
The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
Mandatory because application security decisions must be made within the entity's approved security risk tolerance and documented in the security plan.
Direct - informs risk acceptance for application design, operation, exceptions and residual risks.
3. Security risk appetite and risk acceptance
Agency and Scheme Applications must operate within NDIA's approved security risk appetite, with any exceptions or residual risks documented, approved and reviewed.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Governance, accountability, risk and investment oversight
A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
Required to allocate ownership for each security risk or category of risk, including shared technology and supplier risks.
Direct - applies to application owners, risk owners, platform owners and shared-service arrangements.
3. Security risk appetite and risk acceptance
Each material application security risk must have a named risk owner, accountable treatment owner and review cadence, including shared risks with suppliers or shared platforms.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Governance, accountability, risk and investment oversight
The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
Mandatory because technology risk decisions can affect other entities, interconnected services and shared government capabilities.
Supporting - applies where applications integrate with other entities, shared platforms or whole-of-government services.
3. Security risk appetite and risk acceptance
Risk decisions for Agency and Scheme Applications must consider impacts on connected entities and shared services, and relevant risks must be communicated where appropriate.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit

The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
Procurement and contract decisions must not expose NDIA or government to unacceptable security risk.
Direct - applies to procured applications, SaaS, managed services, development partners and support services.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
Security risk assessment must be completed before procuring or materially changing Agency and Scheme Application products, services or suppliers.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit

Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
Mandatory because contracts must include proportionate security terms requiring suppliers to meet applicable PSPF obligations.
Direct - applies to contracts for application delivery, hosting, integration, development, support and managed services.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
Contracts supporting Agency and Scheme Applications must include security requirements proportionate to information sensitivity, service criticality, integration exposure and PSPF obligations.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit
Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
Required to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF requirements specified by NDIA.
Direct - applies across the application supplier chain and subcontracted services.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
NDIA must define applicable PSPF, ISM and agency security obligations for suppliers and require evidence of compliance across contractors and approved subcontractors.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit

Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
Mandatory because suppliers must report actual or suspected incidents and follow reasonable investigation directions.
Direct - applies to supplier-operated or supplier-supported applications and environments.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
Supplier contracts for Agency and Scheme Applications must require prompt notification of actual or suspected security incidents and cooperation with NDIA incident investigations.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance
Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
Required where government entities provide outsourced services, so consuming entities can review IRAP assurance before use.
Conditional - applies if NDIA consumes or provides government outsourced technology services for applications.
10. Cloud, hosting and outsourced technology assurance
Where NDIA consumes government-provided outsourced technology services for Agency and Scheme Applications, relevant IRAP assessment reports must be obtained and assessed before operational use.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit

Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
Mandatory because contracted security terms must be monitored over the whole contract lifecycle, including subcontractors.
Direct - applies to supplier assurance and contract management for application services.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
NDIA must monitor supplier compliance with contractual security controls for Agency and Scheme Applications throughout the contract lifecycle, including subcontractor controls.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit
Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
Required to ensure security obligations continue through contract completion, transition or termination.
Direct - applies to offboarding, data return, data destruction, access removal and transition of application services.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
Application contracts must include end-of-contract security obligations for transition, data return or disposal, access revocation, records handover and assurance evidence.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit
Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
Mandatory to assess risks from foreign ownership, control or influence before engaging suppliers.
Direct - applies to vendors, cloud providers, outsourced development, support and managed services.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
Procurement for Agency and Scheme Applications must assess supplier foreign ownership, control or influence risks before engagement and document residual-risk decisions.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit
Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
Required because contractual security risks can change and must be reassessed over the life of the arrangement.
Direct - applies to ongoing vendor, SaaS, cloud and managed-service risk management.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
Security risks for application-related contracts must be periodically reassessed and treatments adjusted when services, threats, ownership, architecture or information sensitivity change.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Procurement, supplier risk, contracts, monitoring and exit
Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
Mandatory to use secure and verifiable vendors unless business need requires otherwise and the CISO approves residual risk.
Direct - applies to all third-party application products, platforms, services and integrations.
9. Supplier, procurement and third-party application services
Agency and Scheme Applications must use secure, verifiable third-party vendors and services unless a business-approved exception is risk assessed and residual risk is accepted by the CISO.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
A business continuity plan is developed, implemented and maintained to respond effectively and minimise the impacts of significant business disruptions to the entity's critical services and assets.
Required because critical application services must continue or recover within approved tolerances during significant disruptions.
Direct - applies to business continuity and disaster recovery for critical Agency and Scheme Applications.
NDIA must maintain business continuity and disaster recovery arrangements for critical Agency and Scheme Applications, including recovery objectives, dependencies, testing and evidence.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
The originator remains responsible for controlling the sanitisation, reclassification or declassification of official and security classified information.
Mandatory because originators remain responsible for sanitisation, reclassification and declassification of official and classified information.
Supporting - applies to application workflows that create, manage, transform or disclose official information.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Agency and Scheme Applications must preserve originator responsibilities for reclassification, declassification and sanitisation of official and security classified information.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal

The value, importance or sensitivity of official information is assessed by the originator by considering the potential damage to the government, the national interest, organisations or individuals that would arise if the information's confidentiality were compromised.
Required to assess information value, importance and sensitivity before setting application protections.
Direct - applies to data classification and control selection for application information holdings.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Application owners must assess the value, importance and sensitivity of information processed, stored or communicated by Agency and Scheme Applications before approving controls.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
The security classification is set at the lowest reasonable level.
Mandatory to prevent unnecessary over-classification while ensuring information is appropriately protected.
Supporting - applies to classification decisions in application records, labels and metadata.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Agency and Scheme Applications must support classification decisions at the lowest reasonable level consistent with business, privacy, security and records obligations.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal

Security classified information is clearly marked with the applicable security classification, and when relevant, security caveat, by using text-based markings, unless impractical for operational reasons.
Required so classified information is clearly marked with classification and caveat where relevant.
Direct - applies where applications store, display, export or transmit security classified information.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Applications that handle security classified information must display, store and transmit text-based protective markings and caveats unless impractical for approved operational reasons.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
Mandatory because OFFICIAL and security classified information must receive minimum protections and handling controls.
Direct - applies to application data handling, access, storage, transfer, export and disposal.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Agency and Scheme Applications must apply minimum handling and protection requirements appropriate to the information classification and sensitivity they process.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
Required to apply the Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements for caveated information.
Conditional - applies where applications handle security caveated information.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Applications handling caveated information must enforce caveat-specific handling, access and dissemination requirements set by the controlling authority.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
Security caveats are clearly marked as text and only appear in conjunction with a security classification.
Mandatory to ensure security caveats are visible, text-based and used only with a security classification.
Conditional - applies to applications supporting caveated information, labels, records or exports.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Where caveats are used, Agency and Scheme Applications must ensure caveat markings are text-based, clearly visible and associated with a security classification.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal

The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
Required for technology systems handling classified information to apply AGRkMS Security Classification and Caveat metadata.
Conditional - applies to repositories, workflow systems, records integrations and classified information stores.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Applications that store, process or communicate security classified information must capture and maintain Security Classification and, where relevant, Security Caveat metadata.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
Required where NDIA categorises information by access restrictions using AGRkMS Rights metadata.
Supporting - applies to records, content management and access-control metadata in applications.
6. Information classification, protective marking and metadata
Where access restrictions are categorised, Agency and Scheme Applications must support appropriate Rights metadata to enable consistent restriction, discovery and records management.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
Mandatory because operational controls for information holdings must be proportionate to value, importance and sensitivity.
Direct - applies to all application information holdings and data stores.
Application owners must identify information holdings and implement controls proportionate to their sensitivity, value, business criticality and harm from compromise.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal

OFFICIAL and security classified information is disposed of securely in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements, ISM, the Records Authorities, a Normal Administrative Practice and the Archives Act 1983.
Required to ensure official and classified information in applications is disposed of securely and lawfully.
Direct - applies to application data retention, archival, disposal and secure deletion.
Agency and Scheme Applications must dispose of official and security classified information in line with approved records authorities, retention rules, ISM and handling requirements.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal

Security classified information is appropriately destroyed in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements when it has passed the minimum retention requirements or reaches authorised destruction dates.
Mandatory for destruction of classified information after retention obligations or authorised destruction dates are met.
Conditional - applies where applications store security classified information.
Applications holding security classified information must support authorised destruction processes that meet minimum handling requirements and preserve disposal evidence.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID

Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
Required to ensure external access to classified information occurs only with clearance, need-to-know and approved transfer protections.
Conditional - applies to external access, data exchange and collaboration involving classified information.
External access to classified information in Agency and Scheme Applications must be limited to users with required clearance, need-to-know and approved transfer mechanisms.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
Mandatory because classified information must not be disclosed outside government without an agreement or arrangement.
Conditional - applies to external sharing with non-government organisations, partners, vendors or providers.
Classified information must not be shared through Agency and Scheme Applications with external parties unless an approved agreement or arrangement is in place.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
Mandatory because ASD ISM cyber security principles must be applied throughout each system lifecycle.
Direct - core obligation for design, build, operation, change and retirement of Agency and Scheme Applications.
5. Secure application lifecycle and change management
Agency and Scheme Applications must apply ASD ISM cyber security principles across planning, design, delivery, operation, change and retirement.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
Required to apply ISM controls and cyber security guidelines using a risk-based approach.
Direct - establishes the control baseline and tailoring approach for applications.
5. Secure application lifecycle and change management
Application control baselines must be selected, tailored, implemented and assured using the ISM risk-based approach and documented risk decisions.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift

The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
Mandatory because systems must be authorised to operate before processing, storing or communicating government information.
Direct - applies before go-live, major release, onboarding or production use of applications.
Each Agency and Scheme Application must receive documented authorisation to operate from an Authorising Officer before processing, storing or communicating NDIA or government information.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift
Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
Required so authorisation or reauthorisation decisions are based on the ISM risk-based approach.
Direct - applies to new applications and material changes to existing applications.
Authorisation and reauthorisation decisions must be supported by security assessment evidence, ISM control treatment, residual-risk assessment and documented acceptance.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift
The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
Mandatory because systems must be authorised to the highest classification of information they handle.
Direct - applies to classification of application data, environments, integrations and assurance scope.
Agency and Scheme Applications must be authorised to operate at the highest classification of information they process, store or communicate.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift

A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
Required to maintain an authoritative register of authorised systems and key authorisation decisions.
Direct - applies to the Agency and Scheme Applications inventory and assurance record.
NDIA must maintain a register of authorised Agency and Scheme Applications that records the Authorising Officer, system owner, authorisation date and residual-risk decisions.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift

Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
Mandatory because significant changes or changed security environment can invalidate previous authorisation.
Direct - applies to major functional, architectural, hosting, integration or threat-environment changes.
Applications must be reassessed for authorisation when significant functionality, architecture, hosting, data sensitivity or security-environment changes occur.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Lifecycle, authorisation, register, reassessment and legacy uplift
The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
Required to manage legacy technology that cannot yet be replaced using ASD temporary mitigations.
Direct - applies to legacy applications, unsupported components and technical debt in application estates.
Legacy Agency and Scheme Applications or components that cannot be replaced must have documented temporary mitigations, risk acceptance and retirement or uplift plans.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance

Outsourced facilities that house technology assets and their components with a catastrophic business impact level are certified by ASIO T4 physical security and accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.
Mandatory for catastrophic-impact outsourced facilities to have ASIO T4 certification and ASD accreditation before operational use.
Conditional - applies where applications rely on outsourced facilities for catastrophic business-impact technology assets.
10. Cloud, hosting, gateways and digital infrastructure
Outsourced facilities housing catastrophic-impact application technology assets must not be used operationally unless required physical security certification and ASD accreditation are confirmed.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Classification, records, FOI, electronic transactions and disposal
Technology assets are disposed of securely in accordance with the Information Security Manual.
Required to ensure technology assets are disposed of securely in accordance with the ISM.
Direct - applies to application infrastructure, media, environments, repositories and supporting assets at retirement.
Technology assets supporting Agency and Scheme Applications must be sanitised, destroyed or disposed of securely in accordance with the ISM and retained evidence.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
Patch applications mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory to implement application patching to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Direct - applies to applications, libraries, platforms, containers, SaaS configurations and supporting infrastructure.
11. Cyber security baseline and Essential Eight
Agency and Scheme Applications must meet Essential Eight Maturity Level Two requirements for timely patching of applications and application components.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory to implement multi-factor authentication to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Direct - applies to users, administrators, privileged access and remote access to applications.
11. Cyber security baseline and Essential Eight
Access to Agency and Scheme Applications must use multi-factor authentication consistent with Essential Eight Maturity Level Two and risk-based access requirements.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory to restrict administrative privileges to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Direct - applies to privileged accounts for application administration, support, databases and platforms.
11. Cyber security baseline and Essential Eight
Administrative privileges for Agency and Scheme Applications must be restricted, approved, logged, reviewed and separated from standard user access.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
Application control mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory to implement application control to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Direct - applies to approved software, scripts, application components and execution controls.
11. Cyber security baseline and Essential Eight
Agency and Scheme Application environments must implement application control to permit only authorised software, scripts and executable content.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
User application hardening mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory to implement user application hardening to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Direct - applies to browsers, productivity tools, client-side integrations and application interfaces.
11. Cyber security baseline and Essential Eight
User-facing application environments must be hardened by disabling unnecessary functionality, reducing exploit pathways and applying approved secure configuration baselines.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
Regular back-ups mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory to implement regular backups to Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Direct - applies to application data, configurations, repositories, keys and recovery artefacts.
11. Cyber security baseline and Essential Eight
Agency and Scheme Applications must maintain regular, tested backups of data and configuration needed to restore services within approved recovery objectives.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response

The remaining mitigation strategies from the Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents are considered and, where required, implemented to achieve an acceptable level of residual risk for their entity.
Required to consider remaining ASD mitigation strategies and implement them where needed to reach acceptable residual risk.
Direct - applies to residual application risk treatment beyond the Essential Eight baseline.
11. Cyber security baseline and Essential Eight
Application owners must consider remaining ASD mitigation strategies and implement additional controls where needed to reduce residual application risk to an acceptable level.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance
Cloud Service Providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
Mandatory to use Cloud Service Providers with current IRAP assessments against the latest ISM within the previous 24 months.
Direct - applies to cloud-hosted Agency and Scheme Applications and cloud services used by applications.
10. Cloud, hosting, gateways and digital infrastructure
Cloud services used by Agency and Scheme Applications must have a current IRAP assessment against the latest ISM, completed within the previous 24 months.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance
Entities consider IRAP assessment recommendations and findings, and implement on a risk-based approach.
Required to consider IRAP findings and recommendations using a risk-based approach.
Direct - applies to cloud service selection, onboarding, assurance, exceptions and ongoing risk treatment.
10. Cloud, hosting, gateways and digital infrastructure
IRAP reports for cloud services supporting Agency and Scheme Applications must be reviewed, with findings treated, accepted or monitored through documented risk decisions.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance

Security classified or systems of government significance information and data is securely hosted using a Cloud Service Provider and Data Centre Provider that has been certified against the Australian Government Hosting Certification Framework.
Mandatory for classified or systems-of-government-significance information to be hosted using certified cloud and data centre providers.
Conditional - applies to classified or SOGS data and systems in Agency and Scheme Applications.
10. Cloud, hosting, gateways and digital infrastructure
Classified, high-value or declared systems-of-government-significance information must be hosted only with appropriately certified cloud and data centre providers.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance
The Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel is used when procuring certified data centre space and services.
Required to use the Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel when procuring certified data centre space and services.
Conditional - applies when NDIA procures data centre facilities for application hosting.
10. Cloud, hosting, gateways and digital infrastructure
Procurement of data centre space or services for Agency and Scheme Applications must use mandated whole-of-government panel arrangements where applicable.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance
Internet-connected technology systems, and the data they process, store or communicate, are protected by a gateway in accordance with the ISM and the Gateways Policy.
Mandatory because internet-connected systems and data must be protected by gateways in accordance with the ISM and Gateways Policy.
Direct - applies to internet-facing and internet-connected applications, APIs and services.
10. Cloud, hosting, gateways and digital infrastructure
Internet-connected Agency and Scheme Applications and their data must be protected by approved gateway or security service edge controls aligned to the ISM and Gateway Security Standard.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Cloud, hosting, data centre, gateway and enhanced infrastructure assurance
Gateways or Secure Service Edges that have completed an IRAP assessment (or ASD assessment for TOP SECRET gateways) against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
Required to use gateways or SSEs with recent IRAP or ASD assessment against the latest ISM.
Direct - applies to gateway services protecting application traffic and internet connectivity.
10. Cloud, hosting, gateways and digital infrastructure
Gateways or security service edges protecting Agency and Scheme Applications must have a current IRAP assessment, or ASD assessment where required, against the latest ISM.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Security baseline, logging, resilience, vulnerabilities and incident response
A vulnerability disclosure program and supporting processes and procedures are established to receive, verify, resolve and report on vulnerabilities disclosed by both internal and external sources.
Mandatory to establish vulnerability disclosure processes that receive, verify, resolve and report vulnerabilities.
Direct - applies to externally accessible applications, APIs, portals and supporting services.
NDIA must maintain a vulnerability disclosure process for Agency and Scheme Applications, including intake, triage, verification, remediation, reporting and closure evidence.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
Access to official information is facilitated for entity personnel and other relevant stakeholders.
Required to facilitate appropriate access to official information for entity personnel and relevant stakeholders.
Direct - applies to user access to application information required for business functions.
Agency and Scheme Applications must enable authorised users to access official information needed for their role while applying proportionate controls.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
Appropriate access to official information is enabled, including controlling access (including remote access) to supporting technology systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
Mandatory to enable appropriate access while controlling access, including remote access, to systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
Direct - core access-control obligation for applications and supporting environments.
Access to Agency and Scheme Applications, including remote access, must be authorised, authenticated, limited to business need and monitored.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
Access to security classified information or resources is only given to entity personnel with a need-to-know that information.
Required to ensure classified information access is only provided on a need-to-know basis.
Conditional - applies where applications hold classified information or resources.
Access to classified information in Agency and Scheme Applications must be granted only to personnel with a documented need-to-know.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
Personnel requiring ongoing access to security classified information or resources are security cleared to the appropriate level.
Mandatory because personnel needing ongoing access to classified information must hold the required security clearance.
Conditional - applies to applications that provide ongoing access to classified information or resources.
Ongoing access to classified information in Agency and Scheme Applications must require verification of the appropriate security clearance before access is granted.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID
Personnel requiring access to caveated information meet any clearance and suitability requirements imposed by the originator and caveat controlling authority.
Required because caveated information may have additional clearance and suitability requirements imposed by the originator or caveat authority.
Conditional - applies where applications hold, process or expose caveated information.
Applications handling caveated information must enforce any additional clearance, suitability and caveat authority requirements before access is granted.
Department of Home Affairs / Australian Government
Access control, classified sharing, privileged access and Digital ID

A unique user identification, authentication and authorisation practice is implemented on each occasion where system access is granted, to manage access to systems holding security classified information.
Mandatory to implement unique user identification, authentication and authorisation each time access is granted to systems holding classified information.
Conditional - applies to systems holding security classified information; good practice for all applications.
